14	CASE OD2-DEV2-CONTRA (CONTRA, technical): Night premium shortfalls after the Fenmarch Water payroll cutover
15	Setting: Fenmarch Water is a regional water utility with 2,140 staff. In October 2026 it moved payroll from an in-house legacy system to PayLattice, a hosted payroll platform supplied and configured by Ardentra Ltd. Two parallel-run cycles (August and September) were signed off on 9 October, and a configuration freeze started that day. The board had brought go-live forward by one pay period. The first live payroll was calculated on 27 October and paid on 30 October. Within days, night-shift staff began reporting underpayments. The November calculation is due on 24 November.
16	Presenting request: From Anika Rautio, Chief Operating Officer, 17 Nov: 'Ardentra says our data caused the October pay errors, and Malcolm wants to act on that before the November calculation on 24 Nov. Before I sign anything off, tell me what actually caused the errors, whether Ardentra's account holds up, and which of the proposed actions we should take.'
17	INITIAL EVIDENCE
18	E1 [stage S1] Ardentra incident report AR-INC-2291, G. Vos (Ardentra implementation lead), 10 Nov (vendor-account): Summary: the October underpayments come from source data quality. Our post-incident data audit found 212 employee records with malformed shift-pattern codes (trailing spaces, legacy 'N/S' prefixes). In PayLattice, premium eligibility is driven by shift-pattern code. The production load on 24 Oct used a fresh legacy extract (MD-1023) taken on 23 Oct, which carried these anomalies into production. 18 of the 139 complainants hold flagged records. The rest may carry anomalies that our audit rules do not detect. No change affecting pay calculation was made after parallel-run sign-off (see change log: CR-118 was a label correction). Recommendation: Fenmarch to re-cleanse and reload employee master data before the November run. Under clause 14.3, fixing client-data defects is at Fenmarch's cost.
19	E2 [stage S1] Ardentra-maintained change log extract, 9–28 Oct, supplied with AR-INC-2291 (change-record): CR-114 | 13 Oct | Bank file header field order corrected | calc impact: none | approved O. Calloway (Payroll Manager).
20	CR-118 | 22 Oct | NSP-02 (night shift premium): display label text correction 'Night Prem' → 'Night Shift Premium' | calc impact: none | test: not required | approved O. Calloway (CAB 21 Oct).
21	REL-7.4 | 24 Oct | PayLattice platform release 7.4, includes the statutory tax table update required from the November pay period | calc impact: platform | vendor regression pack passed.
22	CR-121 | 25 Oct | Payslip header logo replaced | calc impact: none.
23	Note: Ardentra consultants write the entries in this log when a change is requested.
24	E3 [stage S1] Payroll helpdesk ticket summary, generated 12 Nov; finance bank reconciliation note, 31 Oct (system-record): October pay tickets: 139, from 139 individuals. Every ticket reports an underpayment, and none reports an overpayment. All 139 cite the night shift premium line. No tickets concern basic pay, overtime, tax or deductions. Shortfalls claimed: £37–£201 per person, median £98. By directorate: Operations (treatment works shift teams) 124; Customer Contact overnight team 15. No tickets from staff who work days only. Finance bank reconciliation for the 30 Oct payment: the amounts credited matched the payroll output file for all 2,140 payees.
25	E4 [stage S1] Email, Malcolm Treharne (Programme Director) to COO, 11 Nov (leadership-account): Ardentra's report makes it clear this is our data. I signed off the cleanse on the strength of the vendor's assurance, and I won't let the November run go wrong for the same reason. My proposal: (1) suspend edit rights for Hannah Lowe's HR data team while the cleanse undergoes a conduct review; (2) re-cleanse and reload the full master data before the 24 Nov calculation; (3) accept the clause 14.3 cost so we don't sour the relationship. Internal audit have asked to look into it, but I don't want to wait for them. Remember that the board brought go-live forward; we can't afford another slip.
26	E5 [stage S1] Interview notes, Priya Dandekar (payroll officer), 12 Nov, taken by internal audit (staff-account): During the parallel run PD checked the night premium for about 40 night workers. All matched the legacy system 'to the penny'. She says the hours on the October payslips she has looked at agree with the rosters: 'it's the premium amount that's short, not the hours.' She knows a few complainants whose shift codes 'have always been messy', but most of the complainants she knows have clean records. On 23 Oct she asked Ardentra whether CR-118 needed testing and was told by email it was 'cosmetic only'. She thinks Ardentra may have reloaded data at cutover but does not know which extract was used.
27	E6 [stage S1] Email, Declan Hurst (Operations Manager) to COO, 14 Nov (manager-account): Voluntary night overtime cover across the treatment works has dropped from 88% of requested shifts (Sept–Oct average) to 61% (1–13 Nov). The night teams are angry about the premium and say so. But the new four-on-four-off rota trial also started on 1 Nov for exactly these teams, and staff reps have complained about both. Honestly, I can't tell which one is driving it. Under the agreement with the reps, the rota trial can be paused at one week's notice. I'm under pressure to pause it now.
28	CATALOGUE (full contents)
29	C1 [stage S1] PayLattice platform configuration audit trail export, tenant FEN-PRD, 1–31 October - Platform audit trail, exported 13 Nov by T. Wierzba (Fenmarch system administrator) (log): Append-only platform audit trail. Tenant users, including Ardentra consultants, cannot edit or delete entries (platform admin guide §9.2). The export was run by Fenmarch's administrator under the read-only audit role. Pay-calculation rule edits, 9–28 Oct: one. 22 Oct 16:41, user imarchetti@ardentra, action 'apply template TPL-NIGHT-STD' to rule NSP-02. Fields changed: display_label 'Night Prem' → 'Night Shift Premium'; window_start 20:00 → 22:00. window_end 06:00 and multiplier 1.33 unchanged. Template TPL-NIGHT-STD (Ardentra library v2) contents: label 'Night Shift Premium', window 22:00–06:00, multiplier 1.33. Other entries: 13 Oct bank file layout (CR-114); 24 Oct release 7.4, 'no tenant rule changes'; 25 Oct payslip image (CR-121). NSP-02 window_start was 20:00 throughout both parallel-run cycles.
30	C2 [stage S1] Internal audit workpapers: parallel-run reconciliation and production data load history - Fenmarch Internal Audit (reports to the Audit Committee), workpaper IA-26-41, 14 Nov (document): The parallel run (August and September cycles) used master data snapshot MD-0915. Night premium was reconciled between legacy and PayLattice for every night-working employee in each cycle (151 in August, 155 in September). No difference exceeded £0.01. 22 of the September night workers hold records on Ardentra's list of 212 flagged records, and all of them reconciled. Production load history (platform job log, extracted by internal audit): on 24 Oct, job LD-PRD-0003 loaded MD-0915 plus 31 starter, leaver and change transactions keyed by Fenmarch payroll. No extract named MD-1023 appears in the job log or in Fenmarch's file-transfer records. None of the 31 transactions relates to night-working staff.
31	C3 [stage S1] Internal audit recalculation of October night premium for all night-working staff - Fenmarch Internal Audit, workpaper IA-26-42, 14 Nov (document): Scope: all 158 staff with night hours in October, not only those who raised tickets. Timesheet hours agreed to the rostering system for 158 of 158. Expected premium follows the collective agreement: time-and-a-third for hours worked 20:00–06:00. Result: 147 underpaid, 11 paid correctly. For each of the 147, the shortfall equals 0.33 × basic hourly rate × hours worked between 20:00 and 22:00, to within £0.01. 8 of the 147 had raised no ticket. The 11 paid correctly are Kelsey Road staff rostered 22:00–06:00. Ardentra flagged list: 19 of 22 flagged night workers were underpaid (86%), against 128 of 136 unflagged (94%). The 190 flagged day workers were paid correctly. Re-run in Ardentra's test tenant (release 7.4, copy of production data) with NSP-02 window_start set to 20:00: all 158 matched expected pay.
32	C4 [stage S1] Ardentra data quality audit: field-level detail of 212 flagged employee records - Ardentra data quality team, 6 Nov (vendor-account): Audit run on 6 Nov against the production tenant using Ardentra's standard data-quality rules. 212 records flagged: 141 shift-pattern codes with trailing spaces (e.g., 'NS4 '); 49 with the legacy prefix 'N/S'; 22 with a missing code effective date. By directorate: Operations 118, Customer Contact 31, Fleet 27, Corporate 36. Ardentra comment: 'Shift-pattern anomalies of this kind commonly cause premium miscalculation in the migrations we have supported.' The audit does not test pay outcomes for the flagged records.
33	C5 [stage S1] Bank payment file and settlement reconciliation, 30 October payment - Fenmarch Finance treasury team, 3 Nov (financial-record): Payment file PF-1030 transmitted 28 Oct 14:02: 2,140 credits, total £5,412,880.16. Bank settlement report, 30 Oct: 2,140 credits settled, identical total, no rejects or returns. Line-level comparison of the payment file with PayLattice net pay output: zero differences. The CR-114 header correction (13 Oct) was in effect, and the bank accepted the file at first submission.
34	C6 [stage S1] Timesheet portal approval timestamps, October pay period - PayLattice timesheet module report, run by Fenmarch payroll, 13 Nov (system-record): October period, 2,140 staff. Timesheets approved after the 26 Oct soft cut-off: night teams 112 of 158 (71%); day teams 431 of 1,982 (22%). Every timesheet was approved before the 27 Oct 09:00 hard lock and processed in the 27 Oct calculation. Timesheets defaulted to contracted hours because they were not approved: 0. Night-team managers say they approve in batches after the last night shift of the period.
35	C7 [stage S1] Written statement of the Ardentra consultant who raised CR-118 - I. Marchetti (Ardentra senior consultant), statement supplied via Ardentra, 13 Nov (vendor-account): On 22 Oct I applied Ardentra's standard night template to NSP-02 so that the label matched our naming standard. I understood the template to set label text, and I did not review the other fields it carries. I described CR-118 as cosmetic in good faith. TPL-NIGHT-STD reflects the configuration most of our clients use. I was not asked to test the change, and the CAB agreed that no test was required. I do not accept that I misrepresented the change.
36	C8 [stage S1] Collective agreement extract (night working), legacy night premium rule specification, and functional design FD-07 - Fenmarch HR policy library and programme document store (document): Collective agreement, Schedule C, para 4: 'A night working premium of time-and-a-third is payable for all hours worked between 20:00 and 06:00.' Legacy payroll rule NPREM (spec v3, 2019): premium = 0.33 × basic hourly rate × hours inside the 20:00–06:00 window. Eligibility depends on the presence of hours in the window. Ardentra functional design document FD-07, signed 2 June, specifies the NSP-02 window as 20:00–06:00.
37	C9 [stage S1] Change advisory board minutes, 21 October - Programme CAB secretary (document): Attendees: M. Treharne (chair), O. Calloway, G. Vos, I. Marchetti, IT service manager. Ardentra presented CR-118 as 'label text correction on NSP-02, no calculation impact, no test required'. A configuration freeze exception was granted on that basis. O. Calloway asked whether payslips would show the new label and was told yes. No field-level preview of the change was presented, and the CAB template does not require one. Approved 4–0.
38	C10 [stage S1] Programme plan revision history and go-live readiness checklist - Programme management office (document): Plan v6 (15 Sept): the programme board brings go-live forward from the November to the October pay period. Readiness checklist signed 9 Oct: parallel run passed (2 cycles); data cleanse signed off by H. Lowe and M. Treharne; configuration freeze in force from 9 Oct, with exceptions through CAB only; hypercare team of 3 Ardentra consultants and 4 Fenmarch payroll staff. Risk R-31, 'compressed testing window after freeze', rated amber; owner M. Treharne.
39	C11 [stage S1] IT service desk incident log, cutover weekend 24–26 October - Fenmarch IT service desk (log): INC-5502, 25 Oct 07:12–07:53: timesheet portal unavailable during the release 7.4 deployment. Restored; transaction replay confirmed no lost or duplicated entries. INC-5507, 25 Oct: payslip PDF header misaligned after the logo change; fixed the same day (CR-121). INC-5511, 26 Oct: two managers unable to log in; passwords reset. No incidents were logged against pay calculation.
40	C12 [stage S1] Sample of 20 payroll helpdesk call recordings, 30 Oct–5 Nov, with listener notes - Payroll helpdesk team leader (staff-account): 20 calls sampled at random from the 139 ticket-raisers. 17 callers describe their night premium as 'short' or 'less than usual'; 3 cannot say what is wrong. 9 calls are angry in tone. Two callers say a colleague told them 'it's the new system's data'. Advice given by the helpdesk in every call: wait for the investigation, and a correction will follow if one is due.
41	C13 [stage S1] Contract schedule 7: clause 14.3 and remediation cost provisions - Fenmarch procurement, Ardentra master services agreement (document): 14.3: 'Costs of remediating a Defect shall be borne by the party whose act or omission caused it. Where a Supplier change was approved by the Client on the basis of a materially accurate description, costs shall be shared equally.' 14.4: disputes go first to the joint steering group, then to mediation. 14.5: neither party may withhold undisputed invoices while a dispute is open.
42	C14 [stage S1] Operations overtime cover dashboard, September–November - Operations performance team (telemetry): Treatment works night overtime, shifts requested and filled: Sept 214/190 (89%); Oct 226/197 (87%); 1–13 Nov 118/72 (61%). Day overtime over the same period: 91%, 90%, 88%. The dashboard records fills only and does not capture reasons for declines. Teams in the rota trial are not identified separately.
43	C15 [stage S1] Payroll officer's parallel-run spot-check spreadsheet, September cycle - P. Dandekar, payroll officer (staff-account): Spreadsheet kept by P. Dandekar. 40 night workers chosen 'from teams I know'. Legacy and PayLattice night premium compared for the September cycle: 40 of 40 equal to the penny. A column note records the data snapshot as 'MD-0915 (per Ardentra email)'. The production load was not checked. No second person reviewed the spreadsheet.
44	C16 [stage S1] October pension contribution file submitted 5 November - Fenmarch payroll, pension scheme submission (financial-record): Pension scheme submission for October: 1,912 members, total pensionable pay £4.31m, with employer and employee contributions calculated by PayLattice. Under scheme rules, night premium is pensionable. The scheme administrator accepted the file on 6 Nov. Corrections to pensionable pay can go in the next monthly file.
45	CANDIDATES
46	H1: The October pay errors stem from inaccurate employee records carried over from the legacy system in the data migration.
47	H2: The October pay errors stem from how pay calculation rules are configured in the new payroll system.
48	H3: The October pay errors stem from hours or shift times recorded incorrectly in the new timesheet portal.
49	H4: The October pay errors stem from the interface that transmits the payment file to the bank.
50	H5: The October pay errors stem from a defect in the new payroll platform's software code.
51	R1: CR-118 edit to night premium rule NSP-02 (22 Oct) -> October night premium underpayments (causes)
52	R2: Malformed shift-pattern codes in migrated employee records -> October night premium underpayments (causes)
53	R3: PayLattice platform release 7.4 (24 Oct) -> October night premium underpayments (causes)
54	R4: October night premium underpayments -> Fall in voluntary night overtime cover in November (causes)
55	A1: Accept Ardentra's attribution: suspend the HR data team's edit rights pending a conduct review, re-cleanse and reload the full employee master data before the 24 Nov calculation, and absorb the remediation cost under clause 14.3.
56	A2: Before the 24 Nov calculation, have Ardentra restore NSP-02's night premium window to its parallel-run setting, verify it by re-running October in the test tenant, and pay every underpaid employee identified by recalculation through an off-cycle payment.
57	A3: Pause the four-on-four-off rota trial now to restore night overtime cover.
58	A4: Roll back PayLattice platform release 7.4 in the production tenant before the November pay run.
59	SCORED ITEMS
60	S1: hypothesis H1 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
61	S2: hypothesis H2 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
62	S3: hypothesis H3 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
63	S4: hypothesis H4 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
64	S5: hypothesis H5 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
65	S6: edge R1 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
66	S7: edge R2 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
67	S8: edge R3 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
68	S9: edge R4 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
69	S10: action A1 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
70	S11: action A2 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
71	S12: action A3 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
72	S13: action A4 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
73	S14: sufficiency SUFF allowed=[sufficient, insufficient]

TPL-NIGHT-STD reflects the configuration most of our clients use. I was not asked to test the change, and the CAB agreed that no test was required. I do not accept that I misrepresented the change.

Legacy payroll rule NPREM (spec v3, 2019): premium = 0.33 × basic hourly rate × hours inside the 20:00–06:00 window. Eligibility depends on the presence of hours in the window. Ardentra functional design document FD-07, signed 2 June, specifies the NSP-02 window as 20:00–06:00.

Calloway asked whether payslips would show the new label and was told yes. No field-level preview of the change was presented, and the CAB template does not require one. Approved 4–0.

Treharne; configuration freeze in force from 9 Oct, with exceptions through CAB only; hypercare team of 3 Ardentra consultants and 4 Fenmarch payroll staff. Risk R-31, 'compressed testing window after freeze', rated amber; owner M. Treharne.

INC-5511, 26 Oct: two managers unable to log in; passwords reset. No incidents were logged against pay calculation.

C13 [stage S1] Contract schedule 7: clause 14.3 and remediation cost provisions - Fenmarch procurement, Ardentra master services agreement (document): 14.3: 'Costs of remediating a Defect shall be borne by the party whose act or omission caused it. H4: The October pay errors stem from the interface that transmits the payment file to the bank.
H5: The October pay errors stem from a defect in the new payroll platform's software code.

R2: Malformed shift-pattern codes in migrated employee records -> October night premium underpayments (causes)
R3: PayLattice platform release 7.4 (24 Oct) -> October night premium underpayments (causes)
R4: October night premium underpayments -> Fall in voluntary night overtime cover in November (causes)

A2: Before the 24 Nov calculation, have Ardentra restore NSP-02's night premium window to its parallel-run setting, verify it by re-running October in the test tenant, and pay every underpaid employee identified by recalculation through an off-cycle payment.
A3: Pause the four-on-four-off rota trial now to restore night overtime cover.
A4: Roll back PayLattice platform release 7.4 in the production tenant before the November pay run.

answers.justification: Production loaded the parallel-run snapshot MD-0915 and there is no MD-1023 (C2). Flagged records were underpaid at a lower rate than unflagged ones (86% vs 94%), and flagged day workers and flagged parallel-run night workers were paid correctly (C3, C2).

The append-only audit trail shows NSP-02's window_start changed from 20:00 to 22:00 on 22 Oct (C1). Every shortfall equals 0.33 × rate × hours worked between 20:00 and 22:00, and restoring 20:00 fixes all 158 cases (C3), against the 20:00 window set by the agreement and FD-07 (C8).
Hours agreed to the rosters for 158 of 158 staff (C3, E5), no timesheets defaulted to contracted hours (C6), and the portal outage lost no entries (C11).
The payment file and bank settlement matched PayLattice net pay with zero differences and no rejects (C5, E3), so the bank interface faithfully passed on already-wrong amounts.

Release 7.4 made no tenant rule changes (C1), and with release 7.4 still running, setting window_start back to 20:00 in the test tenant gave correct pay for all 158 (C3), so the fault is configuration, not platform code.

The edit came before the payroll (C1), the shortfall matches the 20:00–22:00 hours exactly and spares Kelsey Road staff rostered 22:00–06:00 (C3), the data rival is ruled out (C2, C3), and reversing the change in the test tenant fixes every case (C3).

Flagged records were not over-represented among the underpaid (C3), flagged day workers and 22 flagged parallel-run night workers were paid correctly (C3, C2), and the claimed MD-1023 load never happened (C2).
Release 7.4 made no tenant rule changes (C1), and October recalculated correctly under 7.4 once the window was fixed (C3).

Night overtime cover fell after the underpayments while day cover held (C14, E6), but the rota trial for the same teams started on the same date and the dashboard cannot separate them or record reasons (E6, C14).

It punishes the HR data team for errors the data did not cause (C2, C3), leaves the NSP-02 misconfiguration in place for November (C1), and accepts costs that clause 14.3 would place on Ardentra or at least share (C13, C7, C9).
It fixes the confirmed cause (C1, C3) using a verification method already shown to work (C3), and the off-cycle payment based on recalculation covers the 8 underpaid staff who raised no ticket (C3).
The overtime drop cannot yet be pinned on the rota trial rather than the pay errors (E6, C14), so pausing the trial now commits to an unconfirmed explanation.
Release 7.4 did not cause the errors (C1, C3), and it carries the statutory tax table update required from the November period (E2), so rolling it back would introduce tax errors.
The tamper-proof audit trail (C1), the exact recalculation and test-tenant re-run (C3), and the ruling-out of the data explanation (C2) are enough to commit to A2 before 24 Nov.

ambiguousItems: S9: 'association-only' or 'unknown' are both defensible, because the overtime drop is confounded with the rota trial and there is no team-level split (C14, E6).
S12: 'premature' or 'acceptable' are both defensible, because pausing the rota trial is low-cost and reversible at one week's notice (E6), even though its causal role is unconfirmed.
S5: 'contradicted' or 'unknown' are both defensible, since evidence against a code defect rests mainly on one test-tenant re-run (C3) plus the release log (C1).
caseProblems: C3's title, 'recalculation of October night premium for all night-working staff', together with its 'Re-run in Ardentra's test tenant' finding, effectively resolves H2, R1 and the A2 verification in a single item, so the case depends heavily on one decisive workpaper.
A2 does not mention correcting pensionable pay in the next pension file (C16), so a fully correct remediation is somewhat underspecified; this is minor.

Minor numerical check: E1 says 18 of 139 complainants hold flagged records, while C3 shows 19 flagged night workers underpaid. This is consistent if one non-complainant is flagged, but the reader has to infer that.
